A Petition of the Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, Owners and Proprietors of Lands and Grounds, and otherwise interested in the Common and Open Fields, Meadows, Commonable Lands, and Waste Grounds, in the Manor and Parish of Shelton, in the County of Bedford, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Lands and Grounds of the Petitioners, and others, in the said Fields and Meadows, lie intermixed and dispersed, and, in their present Situation, are incapable of Improvement, and it would tend greatly to the Advantage of all Persons interested in the said Common and Open Fields, Meadows, Commonable Lands, and Waste Grounds, if the same were divided and inclosed: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for dividing and inclosing the said Common and Open Fields, Meadows, Commonable Lands, and Waste Grounds, in such Manner as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill, pursuant to the Prayer of the said Petition: And that Mr. Hobart and Mr. Jenkinson do prepare, and bring in, the same.

A Petition of several of the Commissioners for car-

?ing into Execution an Act of Parliament, of the welfth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for embanking, draining, and preserving, certain Fen Lands and Low Grounds, in the Parish of Ramsey, in the County of Huntingdon, and in the Parishes of Doddington, March, Benwick, Wimblington, and Chatteris, within the Isle of Ely in the County of Cambridge, and for amending the Road from a certain Bridge in the Parish of Chatteris aforesaid, called Carter's Bridge, by a Drain, called Vermuyden's, or The Forty Feet Drain, to a Bridge called The Forty Feet Bridge, in the said Parish of Ramsey, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Term of so much of the said Act as relates to the said Road will expire at the End of the present Session of Parliament, and, unless the Term is enlarged, the said Road cannot be kept in good Repair, which will be a great Inconvenience to Persons having Occasion to travel along the same: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to continue the Term and Powers of so much of the said Act as relates to the said Road, for such Time as the House shall think proper.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the same, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Mr. Charles Yorke, General Adeane, &c.: And they are to meet Tomorrow

Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's Chamber; and have Power to send for Persons, Papers, and Records.

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, on Behalf of themselves, and others, being legal Electors of Members to serve in Parliament for the Town and Port of Seaford, in the County of Sussex, was delivered in at the Table, and read; Setting forth, That, upon the 19th Day of March 1792, the Select Committee, who were appointed to try and determine the Merits of a Petition of Sir Godfrey Webster, Baronet, and John Tarleton, Esquire, against the Return of Members to serve in Parliament for the said Town and Port of Seaford, reported to the House, that VOL. 49.

they had determined, " That the Right of Election is m " the Inhabitants, Housekeepers of the said Town and " Port, paying Scotland Lot, and in such Inhabitants " Housekeepers only; " and that the Petitioners are advised, that the said Right of Election, so determined by the said Select Committee, is not the Right of Election for the said Town and Port: And therefore, to prevent the said Judgment of the said Select Committee from becoming final and conclusive, praying, That they may be admitted as Parties, according to the Form of the Statute in that Case lately made and provided, to oppose the said Right of Election, in Favour of which the said Select Committee have reported as aforesaid, and that they may have such other Relief in the Premises as to the House shall seem meet, and the Nature of the Case may require.

Ordered, That the said Petition be taken into Consideration upon Monday the 10th Day of March next, at Three of the Clock in the Afternoon.

Ordered, That Mr. Speaker do issue his Warrant, Or Warrants, for such Persons, Papers, and Records, as shall be thought necessary, by the Parties, on the Hearing of the Matter of the said Petition.

Memorandum:

That Notice of the said Petition, and of the Time appointed for taking the same into Consideration, was inserted, by the Order of Mr. Speaker, in The London Gazette, and also sent to the Returning Officer of the Town and Port of Seaford, according to the Directions of an Act, passed in the 1 wenty-eighth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty; for the further Regulation of the Trials of controverted Elections, or Returns of Members to serve in Parliament.

Martis, 28° d Januarii;

Anno 34° Georgii III*" Regis, 1794. Prayers.

A PETITION of several Trustees for putting in execution an Act of Parliament, made in the Thirty-first Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for more effectually amending, widening, and repairing the Road through the several Parishes of Saint Michael, Saint Alban, Saint Peter, Shenley, Ridge, and South Mims, in the Counties of Hertford and Middlesex, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners^in the Thirty-first Year of His present Majesty's Reign,- obtained an Act to enable them to divert and change the said Road at the Entrance into the Town of Saint Alban (so as to avoid certain steep Hills and sharp Turnings, which render the said Road dangerous for Carriages and Pessengers) and for other Improvements; and that the Petitioners have had several Meetings, in order to put the said Act in execution, and for the Purpose of making the said intended new Road into the Town of Saint Alban, and it appears, from several Surveys which have been made, that the same cannot be executed in a proper Manner, without taking down certain Buildings or Tenements, held in Trust for the Church and Poor of the Parishes of Saint Alban and Saint Peter (that is to say) a small Part of a Tenement in the Occupation of James Fitch, which said Tenement, together with other Premisses, are let at the Yearly Rent of Eleven Pounds, One other Tenement, in the Occupation of the Widow Birch, let at the Yearly Rent of Six Pounds, One other Tenement, in the Occupation of Joseph Cogdell, let at the Yearly Rent of Four Pounds, One other Tenement, in the Occupation of Joseph Siggins, let at the Yearly Rent of Five Pounds, a certain Warehouse and Stable, in the Occupation of Mr. William Hawson, let at the Yearly Rent of Five Pounds, with the Yard thereunto belonging, as also a small Slip of Garden Ground, in the Occupation of Mrs. Smith; and that Application has been made to the acting Trustees of the said Charity, offering to purchase the said Buildings and Premisses at a fair Valuation, but that One out of Six of the said Trustees absolutely refuses to sell or convey the said Tenements and Premisses for the Purposes aforesaid, whereby the Petitioners are rendered unable to carry the intended Improvement into Effect, being restrained, by the said Act, from taking down Buildings without the Consent of the Owners: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to enlarge the Powers of the said Act, and to authorize the Petitioners to take down the said Buildings, and to take in the said Yard and Piece of Garden, making a fair and reasonable Satisfaction to the Trustees of the said Charity, and their Under Tenants, for their respective Interests therein, in such Manner as the House shall think proper.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Condsideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the same, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Mr. Plumer, Mr. John Calvert, Senior, &c.: and they are to meet Tomorrow Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's Chamber; and have Power to send for Persons, Papers, and Records.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr. William Bennett, an Engineer tod Surveyor, being examined, said, That he hath surveyed the Line of the intended Navigation, whereby it appears, that the extending, cutting, and making the Manchester, Bolton and Bury Canal navigable from Bury, by Rochdale and Lit-tleborough, to a certain Place at or near Sladen, and also from Bolton, to a Place at or near Red Moss, at in the County Palatine of Lancaster, would facilitate and render cheap the Conveyance of Merchandize brought into, manufactured, and consumed in the aforesaid Towns, and the adjacent Country, and the produce thereof would afford particular Advantages to the Petitioners, by promoting Agriculture and Commerce, and be of Public Utility: — And he further said, that such Extensions of Canal may be easily effected.

Memorandum:

By the Act passed in 1781, intituled, An Act for establishing an Agreement with the United Company of " Merchants of England trading to the East Indies, &c." the East India Company are required to pay a certain Sum of Money, which is specified in the said Act, in Proportion to the Number of Troops sent, or to be sent, to the East Indies, on the Requisition of the said Company.

This Sum the said Company claim, under the Words of the Act, a Right of paying in the East Indies only: And, as it will be necessary to provide for the Subsistence of the Additional recruiting for the Regiment of Light Dragoons, and of the Recruiting Companies remaining in Great Britain, there will be wanting at present for this Purpose the Sum of £. 8,323. 17. 10 j.; which it will be necessary to vote on Account of the above Estimate.

Ordered, That the said Estimate do He upon the Table, to be perused by the Members of the House.

Ordered, That Colonel Egerton do make the Report from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the several Gentlemen, Clergy, Merchants, Tradesmen, Manufacturers, Land Owners, and others, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, was referred.

Colonel Egerton accordingly reported from the said Committee, That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Navigation Bills, had been complied with; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, which they had directed to be reported to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr. John Rennie, an Engineer, being examined, said, That it is practicable to make a Canal for the Navigation of Boats, Barges, and other Vessels, from and to communicate with the Calder and Hebble Navigation, at or near Sowerby Bridge Wharf, within the Parish of Halifax, in the West Riding of the County of York, by Way of Todmorden, Deyne-head, Littleborough, and Rochdale, to Manchester, and to communicate with the Vo l. 49.

Canal of his Grace the Duke of Bridgewater, at or deaf a Place called Castle Field, within the Parish of Manchester, in the County Palatine of Lancaster, and also certain Navigable Branches from such intended Canal, in the Township of Castleton, in the Parish of to or near a certain Highway called School-land, in the said Parish, and another to or near a Place called Hol-linwood, in the Parish of Prestwick cum Oldham, in the said County Palatine.

That the making and maintaining such Canal and Branches will be the Means of opening a Communication for the Conveyance of Goods, Wares, and Merchandize, Coals, Stone, and Slate, between the East Sea at Hull, and the West Sea at Liverpool, whereby the Trade and Manufactures of many intermediate Towns and Places will be greatly promoted and facilitated, and the Agriculture of a very populous Country materially assisted, by being supplied with Lime and other Manure at a moderate Expence; and that the said Canal, by its Junction with the Canal of the Duke of Bridgewater, will open an inland Navigable Communication with the City of London, the Towns of Lancaster and Kendal, the several Counties of Stafford, Warwick, and Leicester, as well as with the Port of Bristol, and the Towns upon the River Severn, and will be of great Public Utility.

Ordnance

Service-.

'Committee on American Trade Acts.

Sported.

Sill ordered.

64

28° Januani. . 1794.

Mr. William Croslei/being examined, confirmed the Whole of the above Evidence.

Mr. James Holland, Mr. Thomas Fildes, and Mr. Isaac Jackson, being examined, confirmed so much of the Evidence of Mr. Rennie, as relates to the Advantages to be derived from the said Canal.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal from the Colder Navigation, at or near Bridge

Wharf, in the Parish of Halifax, in the West Riding of the County of York, to join the Canal of his Grace the Duke of Bridgewater, in the Parish of Manchester, in the County Palatine of Lancaster, and also certain Cuts from the said intended Canal: And that Colonel Egerton and Mr. Blackburne do prepare, and bring in, the same.

Ordered, That the Order of the Day, for the House to resolve itself into a Committee of the whole House, to consider of an Act, made in the Twenty-third Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act for preventing certain Instruments from " being required from Ships belonging to the United " States of America, and to give to His Majesty, for " a limited Time, certain Powers for the better carrying on Trade and Commerce between the Subjects of His Majesty's Dominions and the Inhabitants of the said United States and also, of an Act, made in the Twenty-fourth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act to extend the Powers of an Act, made in the Twentythird Year of His present Majesty, for giving His Majesty certain Powers for the better carrying on " Trade and Commerce between the Subjects of His Majesty's Dominions and the Inhabitants of the " United States of America, to the Trade and Commerce of this Kingdom with the British Colonies " and Plantations in America, with respect to certain " Articles therein mentioned and also, of an Act, made in the last Session of Parliament, intituled, "An Act to continue the Laws now in Force for regulating the Trade between the Subjects of His Majesty's Dominions and the Inhabitants of the " Territories belonging to the United States of America, " so far as the same relate to the Trade and Commerce " carried on between this Kingdom and the Inhabitants " of the Countries belonging to the said United States," be now read.

And the said Order being read accordingly;

The House resolved itself into the said Committee.

Mr. Speaker left the Chair.

Mr. Hobart took the Chair of the Committee.

Mr. Speaker resumed the Chair.

Mr. Hobart reported from the Committee, That he was directed by the Committee to make a Motion, when the House will please to receive the same.

Ordered, That the Report be now received.

Mr. Hobart accordingly reported from the said Committee, That he was directed by the Committee to move the House, that Leave be given to bring in a Bill to continue the Laws now in Force for regulating the Trade between the Subjects of His Majesty's Dominions and the Inhabitants of the Territories belonging to the United States of America, so far as the same relate to the Trade and Commerce carried on between this Kingdom and the Inhabitants of the Countries belonging to the said United States.

And Mr. Hobart moved the House accordingly.

MR. Blackburne presented to the House, accord-

ing to Order, a Bill for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal from the Navigation, at or

near Sowerby Bridge Wharf, in the Parish of Halifax, in the West Riding of the County of York, to join the Canal of his Grace the Duke of Bridgewater, in the Parish of Manchester, in the County Palatine of Lancaster, and also certain Cuts from the said intended Canal: And the same was received; and read the First Time.

Resolved, That the Bill be read a Second Time.

A Petition of the Governors and Guardians of the Hospital for the Maintenance and Education of exposed and deserted Young Children, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners are possessed of certain Pieces of Ground within the Parishes of Saint Pancras, Saint George the Martyr, and Saint George Bloomsbury, in the County of Middlesex, situate near the said Hospital, containing Fifty-six Acres, or thereabouts; and that the Petitioners have entered into Agreements with divers Persons for laying out and building several Streets, and other Public Passages and Places upon the said Ground, and several Houses have been already erected thereon, and the Petitioners propose to let the Remainder of the said Ground for the like Purpose, or the greatest Part thereof: And representing to the House, that, if proper Provision was made for paving, cleansing, lighting, watching, and watering, the several Streets, and other Public Passages and Places, which have been, and may be, set out and made upon the said Qround, and for preventing Nuisances, Encroachments, Obstructions, and Annoyances therein, the same would be of great Benefit, Safety, and Convenience to all Persons residing the rein, and resorting thereto, and, by inducing other Persons to take Building Leases, would greatly improve the value of the said Charity Estate: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for paving, cleansing, lighting, watching, and watering, the several Streets, and other Public Passages, and Places, which have been, and may be, set out and made over or upon the said Ground, and for preventing Nuisances, Encroachments, Obstructions, and Annoyances therein, in such Manner as the House shall think proper.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the same, as it hall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Mr. Mainwaring, Mr. Hobart, &c.: And they are to meet upon Friday Morning next, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's Chamber; and have Power to send for Persons, Papers, and Records.

A Petition of the Gentlemen, Merchants, Manufacturers, and Inhabitants, of the Towns of Warwick and Birmingham, and of the County of Warwick, and other Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That, by Levels, Surveys, and Estimates, lately taken and made, it appears, that a Canal, navigable for Boats, and other Vessels of heavy Burthen, may be made from the Warwick and Birmingham Canal, at or near

Warwick, to the Oxford Canal at Braunston, in the County of Northampton; and that the making such Vol. 49.

Canal will open a very near Communication by Water between the Town of Birmingham and the Oxford Canal and Grand Junction Canal at Braunston afore-saidt and be the Means of increasing the Trade and Commerce of the said County of Warwick in general, and of the said Towns of Warwick and Birmingham in particular; and will likewise be of great Public Utility: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal from the Warwick and Birmingham Canal, at of near Warwick, to the Oxford Canal at Braunston aforesaid, under'such Regulations as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the same, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Sir John Mordaunt, Mr. Gilbert, &c.: And they are to meet upon F'riday Morning next, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's Chamber; and have Power to send for Persons, Papers, and Records.

Mr. Pluma' reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of several Trustees for putting in execution an Act of Parliament, made in the Thirty-first Year of the Reigti of His present Majesty, for more effectually amending, widening, and repairing, the Road through the several Parishes of Michael, Saint Albany Saint Peter, Shenley, Ridge, and South Mims, in the Counties of Hertford and Middlesex, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Turnpike Bills, had been complied with; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the same, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report iti his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same wa6 read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, the said Act was read; by which the said Trustees w'ere enabled to divert and change the said Road at the Entrance into the Town of Saint Alban, to avoid certain steep Hills and sharp Turnings, which render the said Road dangerous for Carriages and Passengers; and to make other Improvements: And,

Mr. Thomas Cumber, Clerk to the Trustees, being examined, said, That the Trustees have had several

Meetings in order to put the said Act in execution, and for the purpose of making the said intended new Road into the Town of Saint Alban; and that it appears, from several Surveys which have been made, that the same cannot be executed in a proper Manner without taking down certain Buildings or Tenements, as described in the Petition, and which are held in Trust for the Church and Poor of the Parishes of Saint Alban and Saint Peter. — The Witness further said, That Application has been made to the acting Trustees of the said Charity, offering to purchase the said Buildings and Premises at a fair Valuation, but that One out of Six of the said acting Trustees absolutely refuses to sell or convey the said Tenements and Premises for the Purposes aforesaid; whereby the Trustees of the said Road are rendered unable to carry the intended Improvement into Effect, being restrained, by the said ^ct, from taking down Buildings, without the Consent of the Owners.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill to enable the Trustees for the Care of the Road through the several Parishes of Saint Michael, Saint Alban, Saint

Peter, Shenley, Ridge, and South in the Counties of Hertford and Middlesex, to change the Course of the said Road, at the Entrance into the Town of Saint Alban:

And that Mr. Plumer, Mr. Baker, and Mr. Calvert, Senior, do prepare, and bring in, the same.

A Petition of the Company of Proprietors of the Birchillaixi Wyrley and Essi/igton Canal Navigation, was presented Huddleston* to the House, and read; Setting forth, That, by an Act passed in the Thirty-second Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, the Petitioners were authorized to make a Navigable Canal from, or from near, Wyrley Bank, in the County of Stafford, to communicate with the Birmingham and Birmingham and Canal, at

or near the Tow n of Wolverhampton, in the said County, and also several Collateral Cuts to communicate therewith, and the said Canal and Collateral Cuts are nearly completed according to the Directions of the said Act; and that the Petitioners have caused Levels and Surveys to be taken, whereby it appears that a Navigable Canal may be made from the said Wyrley and Canal at c r near Birchill, in the Parish of Walsall, to join the Coventry Canal at or near in the same County, and also a Navigable Cut from or out of the intended Canal at or near Little Bloxwich, in the Parish of Walsall, into certain Lands called The Lord's Hayes, in the Liberty of Wyrley, belonging to the Marquis of Stafford; and that the making the said Canal and Cut, together with proper Reservoirs, Railw ays, and other Works and Roads, to communicate therewith, will open Navigable Communications with several valuable and extensive Mines of Coal, Ironstone, and Limestone, upon and near the Line of the said Canal and Cut, and will be of very great Benefit to the Owners thereof, and also to the several Persons residing or having Estates in that Part of the Country, and of Public Utility; and the Petitioners are willing to undertake the making such Navigable Canal and Cut as aforesaid, in case they shall be authorized so to do by Authority of Parliament: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to enable them to make and maintain such Navigable Canal and Cut as aforesaid, with proper Railways and other Roads to communicate therewith, in such Manner, and under such Regulations, as the House shall think proper.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the same, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to the Earl Goicer, Mr. Gilbert,

&c.: And they are to meet Tomorrow Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's Chamber; and have Power to send for Persons, Papers, and Records.

New Sarum A Petition of the Victuallers and Innkeepers of the and^nnk" City of New Sarum, in the County of Wilts, was pre-n» PetitlonT* sented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the said City, from its Central Situation in the Western Counties of England, is subject to the serious Burthen of great Numbers of the Army, both Horse and Foot, which must inevitably pass through it in their usual Routes, besides the heavy Load of One or more Regiments, and especially of Horse, which are therein almost constantly quartered, and the same has been found, on Account of such Situation, to be in a more particular Manner oppressive to the Petitioners than to the Victuallers and Innkeepers of most other Cities and principal Towns in the-.Kingdom, inso much that it is impossible for them to carry on their Business* and to maintain themselves and Families, without rsome effectual Relief; and that Barracks for the Accommodation of the Army, where Troops have heretofore been usually quartered on the Victuallers and Innkeepers of many Cities and Towns, have been built, or are now building, to their great Relief: And therefore praying, That the House will take the Premises into Consideration, and take such Measures for the Relief of the Petitioners, either by causing to be built and erected for the Use of such of His Majesty's Forces as may be resident in, or pass through, the said City, Such convenient Barracks as may be sufficient for those Purposes, or by such other Measures as to the House may seem most expedient for redressing the very heavy Grievance and Oppression which at present the Petitioners particularly labour under.

Ordered, That fthe said Petition do lie upon the Table.

And the said Petition was read; Setting forth, That the principal Avenue of Communication between the Cities of London and Westminster, by Temple Bar, and the other Avenue, between the City of London and the New Buildings towards the North and West, by Snow Hill, are much too narrow for the increased Trade and Population of the Metropolis, and very incommodious and dangerous to Passengers; and that the Petitioners conceive, that the widening and improving the said Passages, and making proper Communications therewith, would be a very great Advantage and Accommodation to the Public in general, and afford additional Security to the Lives and Property of His Majesty's Subjects: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for widening and improving the said Passages, and making proper Communications therewith, and for defraying the Expence thereof, in such Manner as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Motion was made, and the Question being pro-11 posed, That the Copy of the Treaty between His Majesty and the King of Sardinia, signed at London the 25th of April 1793, and Translation (which were presented to the House upon the 17th Day of June in the last Session of Parliament) be referred to the said Committee;

The House was moved, That the Entry in the Journal of the House, of the 9th Day of January 1743, of the Translation of His Majesty's Ratification of the Treaty concluded at Worms the -rV September 1743, might be read.

And the same was read accordingly.

Rowland, Joseph Yeoward, Ralph Elliot, and Joseph Brownrigg, Citizens of the City of Carlisle, was delivered in at the Table, and read; Setting forth, That by a late Resolution of a Select Committee of this House, appointed to try the Merits of the Petition of John Christian Curwen and Wilson Braddyll, Esquires, complaining of an undue Election and Return of the City of Carlisle, in the County of Cumberland, and which, on the 3d Day of March 1791, was by them reported to the House, that the Right of Election for the City of Carlisle, in the County of Cumberland, is declared to be in the Freemen of the said City, duly admitted and sworn Freemen of the said City, having been previously admitted Brethren of one of the Eight Guilds or Occupations of the said City, and deriving their Title to spch Freedom by being Sons of Freemen, or by Service of Seven Years Apprenticeship to a Freeman, resident during such Apprenticeship within the said City, and in no others; and that the Petitioners are not satisfied with the said Resolution, and are desirous of being admitted Parties to oppose such Right of Election, and to have the Benefit of the Statute in that Case made and provided: And therefore praying the House to take the Premises into Consideration, and to grant the Petitioners such Relief therein as the House shall think fit.

Ordered, That the said Petition be taken into Consideration upon Monday, the 17th Day of March next, at Three of the Clock in the Afternoon.

Ordered, That Mr. Speaker do issue his Warrant, or Warrants, for such Persons, Papers, and Records, as shall be thought necessary, by the Parties, on the Hearing of the Matter of the said Petition.

Petition from certain Electors of Westminster respecting the Right of Election.

bunas, 5° die Februarii;

Anno 34® Georgii IIItil Regis, 1794. Prayers.

LORD Viscount Stopford reported to the House, That their Address of Friday last (that His Majesty would be graciously pleased to give Directions, that the Account therein mentioned might be laid before this House) had been presented to His Majesty; and that His Majesty had commanded him to acquaint this House, that He will give Directions accordingly.

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, Electors of Members to serve in Parliament for the City and Liberty of Westminster, was delivered in at the Table, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners observe, by the Votes of the House, that the Select Committee, lately appointed to try and determine the Merits of a Petition of Sir Samuel Hood, Baronet, Lord Hood in the Kingdom of Ireland; and also a Petition of several Inhabitants, Householders of the City and Liberty of Westminster, paying Scotland Lot, severally complaining of an undue Election for the said City and Liberty, did, on the 6th day of July 1789, report to this House, " That it appeared to the said Select Committee, that " the Merits of the Petitions did, in Part, depend upon " the Right of Election; the Parties were therefore required to deliver in Statements, in Writing, " of the Right of Election for which they respectively " contended: That, in Consequence thereof, the Petitioner, Lord Hood, delivered in a Statement, as " follows: — " The Petitioner, Lord Hood, states the *< Right of Election, for the City and Liberty of Westminster is in the Inhabitants, Householders paying " Scotland Lot, within the United Parishes of Saint " Margaret and Saint John, and the several Parishes " of Saint Paul Covent Garden, Saint Ann, Saint James, " Saint George Hanover Square, and the Liberty of " Saint Martin Le Grand, in the County of Middlesex, " and in so much of the Parishes of Saint Martin in the Fields, Saint Clement Danes, and Saint Mary le " Strand, as are not within any of the Four Wards of " the Liberty of the Dutchy of Lancaster, called The " Temple Bar Ward, The Royal Ward, The Middle " Ward, and Precinct of the Savoythat the Electors " Petitioners delivered in a Statement, as follows — " The Electors Petitioners state, That the Right of " Election for the City and Liberty of Westminster is " in the Inhabitants, Householders paying Scotland " Lot, within the united Parishes of Saint Margaret " and Saint John, in the several Parishes of Saint Paul Covent Garden, Saint Ann, Saint James, Saint George " Hanover Square, in the Liberty of Saint Martin le " Grand in the County of Middlesex, and in so much " of the Parishes of Saint Martin in the Fields, Saint " Clement Danes, and Saint Mary le Strand, as are not " within any of the Four Wards of the Liberty of the " Dutchy of Lancaster, called, The Temple Bar Ward, " The RoyalWard, The Middle Ward, and Precinct of " the Savoy;" that the Sitting Member, Lord John " Townshend, delivered in a Statement, as follows — " The Right of Election is in the Inhabitants, Householders of the Parishes of Saint Margaret and Saint " John, Saint George Hanover Square, Saint James " Westminster, Saint Martin in the Fields, Saint Clement

" Danes, Saint Mary le Strand, Saint Mary le Savoy, " Saint Paul Covent Garden, Saint Ann Soho, and the " District of Saint Martin le Grand;" — That, upon the " Statement delivered in by the Petitioners, the said " Select Committee have determined, " That the " Right of Election for the City and Liberty of Westminster is in the Inhabitants, Householders paying " Scotland Lot, within the United Parishes of Saint " Margaret and Saint John, and the several Parishes " of Saint Paul Covent Garden, Saint Ann, Saint James, " Saint George Hanover Square, in the Liberty of " Saint Martin le Grand in the County of Middlesex, " and in so much of the Parishes of Saint Martin " in the Fields, Saint Clement Danes, and Saint Mary " le Strand, as are not within any of the Four Wards " of the Liberty of the Dutchy of ." — That,

" upon the Statement delivered in by the Sitting " Member, the Committee have determined, " That " the Right of Election, as set forth in the said Statement, is not the Right of Election for the said City " and Liberty of Westminster;" and that the Petitioners are advised, and humbly insist, that the Right of Election, which hath been deemed valid in the Judgment of the said Select Committee, is not the ancient and'true Right of Election for the said City and Liberty: And therefore praying, That they may be admitted as Parties to oppose the Right of Election, which has been deemed valid in the Judgment of the said Select Committee, and that the Petitioners may have such further and other Relief in the Premises, as to the House shall seem meet, and the Nature of the Case may require.

Ordered, That the said Petition be taken into Consideration upon Thursday, the 20th Day of March next, at Three of the Clock in the Afternoon.

Ordered, That Mr. Speaker do issue his Warrant, or Warrants, for such Persons, Papers, and Records, as shall be thought necessary, by the Parties, on the Hearing of the Matter of the said Petition.

ean*‘ to consider of Ways and Means for raising the Supply

granted to His Majesty, be now read.

And the said Order being read accordingly;

The House resolved itself into the said Committee.

Mr. Speaker left the Chair.

Mr. Hobart took the Chair of the Committee.

Mr. Speaker resumed the Chair.

Mr. Hobart reported from the Committee, That they had come to several Resolutions; which they had directed him to report, when the House will please to receive the same.

Ordered, That the Report be received Tomorrow Morning.

Mr. Hobart also acquainted the House, That he was directed by the Committee to move, that they may have Leave to sit again.

Resolved, That this House will, upon Wednesday Morning next, resolve itself into a Committee of the whole House, to consider further of Ways and Means for raising the Supply granted to His Majesty.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for the Regulation of His Majesty's Marine Forces while on Shore: And that Mr. Stephens, the Lord Arden, and Mr. John Smyth, do prepare, and bring in, the same.

Ordered, That the Estimate of the Charge of defraying the Civil Establishment of New South Wales, from the ioth of October 1793 to the 10th of October 1794, be referred to the said Committee.

Then the House resolved itself into the said Committee.

Mr. Speaker left the Chair.

Mr. Hobart took the Chair of the Committee.

Mr. Speaker resumed the Chair.

Mr. Hobart reported from the Committee, That they had come to several Resolutions; which they had directed him to report, when the House will please to receive the same.

Ordered, That the Report be received Tomorrow Morning.

Mr. Hobart also acquainted the House, That he was directed by the Committee to move, that they may have Leave to sit again.

Resolved, That this House will, upon Wednesday Morning next, resolve itself into a Committee of the Vol. 49.

whole House, to consider further of the Supply granted to His Majesty.

The other Order of the Day being read;

Resolved, That this House will, Tomorrow Morning, resolve itself into a Committee of the whole House, upon the Bill to continue the Laws now in Force for regulating the Trade between the Subjects of His Majesty's Dominions and the Inhabitants of the Territories belonging to the United States of America, so far as the same relate to die Trade and Commerce carried on between this Kingdom and the Inhabitants of the Countries belonging to the said United States.

And then the House adjourned till Tomorrow Morning, Ten of the Clock.

A Petition of the W'oolcombers for the County of Somerset-Somerset, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That, by the Invention of a Machine for Petition, combing of Wool, which diminishes Labour to an alarming Degree, the Petitioners entertain just Fears, that they and their Families will speedily become a heavy Burthen to the State, it appearing to the Petitioners, that One Machine only, with the Assistance of One Person and Four or Five Children, will perform as much Labour as Thirty Men in the customary Manual Manner: And hoping that the House will apply such Remedy as to them shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Ordered, That the said Estimate do lie upon the 'Table, to be perused by the Members of the House.

A Petition of she "Committee of the Company df Merchants trading to Africa, being offered to be presented to the House;

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer (by His Majesty's Command) acquainted the House, mat His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought" up, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners have laid before the House, an Account of the Money granted for the Year 1792, examined and passed by the Ciirsitor Baron of the Exchequer, as required by an Act of the Twenty-third of George the Second, intituled, "An Act for extending and improving the Trade to ," and that they have invested the Money, granted in 1793, for the Support and Maintenance of the Forts and Settlements on the said Coast; and that the Petitioners have often represented to the House, that the old Forts and Settlements in Africa, being originally ill constructed, and built of very bad Materials, required continual and great Repairs, that they were delivered to the Petitioners by the late Royal African Company in a very ruinous Condition, and that the Sum usually granted by Parliament, after defraying the necessary Expences of the Civil and Military Establishments, were by no means sufficient to enable the Petitioners to preserve them from falling into Decay; and their Duty now obliges them (however reluctantly) to represent further, that the said usual Grants become still more insufficient for the Support and Maintenance of the said Forts and Settlements, by the Existence of various additional and unavoidable Expences

which they have been put to in the last Year, and which still continues, not only in the increased permanent Charge of their Civil and Military Establishments, but In thetidditiorrtA Expences ib 'Consequence of the present War, as well in Freight and Insurance, as in the Cost of Various Oomtnodrties for the Supply of the 16athe; and that the said increased Expences amount, upon a moderate Estimate, to a Sum not less than £.2,000 per Annum, and the Petitioners are apprehensive that they must be still further augmented, both by an Increase in Number, and in the Salaries of Officers and Servants necessary "to be employed in the said - Forts and Settlements: And that the Petitioners, being sensible of the great Regard shewn by the House for the Preservation, Improvement, and ExtenSioU, of the Trade to Africa, and for the Defence and Maintenance of the British Forts and Settlements on that Coast necessary thereto, therefore pray the House to take the Premises into Consideration, and grant such Sum as may be sufficient, as well for the extraordinary Expences of the last-Year not provided for by Parliament, as for the present Repairs, and for the effectual permanent Support of the said Forts and Settlements, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Mr. Hobart, according to Order, reported from the

Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider further of the Supply granted to His Majesty, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding Five hundred and Fifty-eight thousand and Twenty-one Pounds Eleven Shillings and Three Pence, be granted to His Majesty, for the Ordinary of the Navy, including Half Pay to Sea and Marine Officers, for the Year 1794.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding Five hundred and Forty-seven thousand Three hundred and Ten Pounds, be granted to His Majesty, towards the Buildings, Rebuildings, and Repairs of Ships of War in His Majesty's and the Merchants Yards, and other Extra Works, over and above what are proposed to be done upon the Heads of Wear and Tear and Ordinary, for the Year 1794.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Number of Land Forces, including Three thousand Eight hundred and Eighty-two Invalids, amounting to Sixty thousand Two hundred and Forty-four effective Men, Commissioned and Non-commissioned Officers included, be employed for the Year 1794-

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding One Million Four hundred and Ninety-two thousand Eight hundred and Twelve Pounds Twelve Shillings and Two Pence, be granted to His Majesty, for defraying the Charge of Sixty thousand Two hundred and Forty-four effective Men, for Guards, Garrisons, and other His Majesty's Land Forces, including those in Guernsey and Jersey, in Flanders, on an Expedition under the Command of the Earl of Moira, and on Board the Fleet, including the Charge of the Pay of Commissioned and Non-commissioned Officers and Private Men, the Charge of Cloathing of Non-commissioned Officers and Private Men, the Charge of Agency, and the Charge of Allowances to be made to Captains, Paymasters, Surgeons, Riding Masters, and for Serjeants, from 25th December 1793 to 24th December 1794, both inclusive, being Three hundred and Sixty-five Days.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding Six hundred Seventy-seven thousand Six hundred Eighty-two Pounds Twelve Shillings and Four Pence, be granted to His Majesty, for maintaining His Majesty's Forces in the Plantations, including those in Garrison at Gibraltar, and a Corps of Foot in New South Wales, including the Charge of the Pay of the Commissioned Officers, Non-commissioned Officers, and Private Men, the Charge of Cloathing of the Non-commissioned Officers and Private Men, the Charge of Agency, and the Charge of Allowances to be made to Captains, Paymasters, Riding Master, Surgeons and Serjeants, from 25th December 1793 to 24th December 1794, both inclusive, being Three hundred and Sixty-five Days.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for punishing Mutiny and Desertion, and for the better Payment of the Army and their Quarters: And that Mr. Secretary at War, Mr. Rose, and Mr. Charles Long, do prepare, and bring in, the same.

Mr. Hobart, according to Order, reported from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider of Ways and Means for raising the Supply granted to His Majesty, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, towards raising the Supply granted to His Majesty, the Duties upon Malt, Mum, Cyder, and Perry, which, by an Act of Parliament of the Thirty-third Year of His present Majesty's Reign, have Continuance to the 24th Day of June 1794, be further continued, and charged upon all Malt which shall be made, and upon all Mum which shall be made or imported, and all Cyder and Perry which shall be made for Sale within the Kingdom of Great Britain, from the 23d Day of June 1794 to the 24th Day of June 1795. <ition report- Warwick and Birmingham, and of the County of Warwick, and other Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Navigation Bills, had been complied with; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the same, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition Mr. William Felkyn, being examined, said, That, by Levels and Surveys lately taken, it appears that a Canal, navigable for Boats and other Vessels, may be made from the Warwick and Birmingham Canal, at or near Warwick, to the Oxford Canal at Braunston, in the County of Northampton; that the making such Canal will open a very near Communication by Water between the Town of Birmingham and the Oxford Canal, and the Grand Junction Canal at Braunston aforesaid, and be the Means of increasing the Commerce of the said County of Warwick in general, and of the Towns of Warwick and Birmingham in particular, and w ill be of great Public Utility.

Mr. Charles Handley, being examined, confirmed so much of the above Evidence as relates to the Utility of the proposed Canal.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal out of and from the Warwick and Birmingham Canal, now cutting, or intended to be cut, in the Parish of brooke, in the County of Warwick, into the Oxford Canal in the Parish of Braunston, in the County of Northampton: And that Sir John Mordaunt, the Lord Arden, and Mr. George Villiers, do prepare, and bring in, the same.

Birmingham A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names and Stone are thereunto subscribed, being Trustees for putting Bridge Road in Execution Three Acts of Parliament, passed in the ‘Petition- Eighteenth Year of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the Second, and the Tenth and Twenty-eighth Years of His present Majesty's Reign, for repairing the Road from Birmingham, in the County of Warwick (through ElmdonJ to a Lane leading by the End of Stone Bridge, in the said County, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That great Progress hath been made in amending the said Road, in the doing of which, a very considerable Debt hath been contracted, but several Parts thereof still remain narrow and incommodious, and in a ruinous and bad Condition; and that the said Debt cannot be paid off, and the Road be effectually amended, widened, and kept in Repair, unless the Term of the said Acts be continued, and the Powers thereof altered and enlarged: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for the Purposes aforesaid, in such Manner, and under such Regulations, as to the House shall seem meet.

" and also for making a Navigable Branch from the " said Canal, at or near Galgate, to Glasson Dock, in the said County Palatine of Lancaster" were empowered (exclusive of the Two several Branches in the said first-mentioned Act) to make, complete, and maintain a certain other Navigable Branch from the said Lancaster Canal, commencing at or near Galgate aforesaid, through the several Lands and Grounds therein mentioned, in the Townships of Ellel and Thumham, in the said County Palatine of Lancaster, to be continued to, and communicate with, the Dock at Glasson, within the Port of Lancaster, and the Petitioners are proceeding in the Execution of the said Lancaster Canal Navigation with great Expedition; and that, by a Survey lately taken, it appears that an Extension of the said Lancaster Canal Navigation may be made from the said Lancaster Canal, in the Township of Asptil, in the Parish of Wigan, in the said County Palatine of Lancaster, to join and communicate with the Canal Navigation of the Duke of Bridgewater, in the Township of Worsley, in the Parish Vol. 49.

of Eccles, in the said County Palatine of Lancaster, which said Extension, by passing into or through the several Parishes of Wigan, Dean, Leigh, and Eccles, and into or through the several Townships of Aspul,

Ince, West Houghton, Hindley, West Leigh, Atherton, Tildsley, Bedford, Astley, and Worsley, will be not only of great Benefit to the Petitioners, and to all other Persons having Lands and Estates in the Neighbourhood thereof, but also to the Public in general, as it will not only open an easy, safe, and commodious Communication through a populous and trading Country, between the several Towns and Places hereinbefore mentioned, but also will unite the whole Lancaster Canal Navigation, and the several Branches thereof, rich in Coals, Cannel, and Limestone, with most of the Canal Navigations now made, or making, in the more Southern Parts of this Kingdom; and that, if a short Deviation of the Line of the Lancaster Canal Navigation, which remains yet unfinished, was made, commencing from, at, or near, a certain Place called Cabus Nook, in the Township of Cabus, in the said County of Lancaster, to communicate with the said Lancaster Canal Navigation, in the Township of Bamacre with Bonds, in the said County, and which said Deviation would be made and carried into or through the several Parishes of Cockerham and Gar-stang Church Town, and into or through the several Townships of Cabus, Winmarley, Garstang,

and Bamacre with Bonds, it would facilitate the making of the said Lancaster Canal Navigation, and save a very considerable Expence to the Petitioners, and would otherwise be of Public Advantage; and that, in order to make the said intended Extension and Deviation, and to complete the said Lancaster Canal and Branches, it may become necessary that the Petitioners be empowered to borrow and take up at Interest a further Sum of Money upon the Credit of the said Lancaster Canal Navigation; and that the said Acts are, in many Respects, defective, and will require to be amended and rendered more effectual: And therefore praying,

Answer of Mr. Speaker acquainted the House, That he had re-General ceived, from Major General Abercromby, the following Abercromby Letter, in Return to the Thanks of this House, signified Thanks of to by Mr. Speaker, in Obedience to their Commands of the 19th Day of December in the last Session of Parliament:

Bombay, 1st May 1793.

Sir,

I have been honoured with your Letter of the 7th January last, accompanying Resolutions of the House of Commons, by One of which that House has been pleased to confer on me the greatest Honour that a British Subject can receive, namely, the Approbation of his Country.

Permit me, Sir, at the same Time, to offer you my warmest Acknowledgements for the very handsome and polite Manner in which you have had the Goodness to convey to me the Thanks of the House.

I have the Honour to be,

With the greatest Respect,

Sir,

Your most obedient,

and very faithful Servant, Robert Abercromby.

The Right honourable Henry

Addington, Speaker of the House of Commons, &c. &c. &c.

A Petition of several Owners and Proprietors of Compton In-Lands and Grounds in the Common Fields of Little closure 1>e' Compton, in the County of Gloucester, was presented to Utl00‘ the House, and read; Setting forth, That the said Lands and Grounds lie open and intermixed, and are inconveniently situated for the Owners thereof; and that it would tend to the Improvement of the Estates of all Persons interested therein, if the said Lands were to be divided and inclosed, and separate Allotments thereof made to the Owners and other Persons interested therein, according to their respective Shares and Interests: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for dividing and inclosing the said Lands and Grounds, and for allotting the same amongst the Petitioners and all others interested therein, according to their respective Shares and Interests in the same, under such Regulations as to the House shall seem necessary or expedient.

Plymouth A Petition of the Woolcombers of Plymouth, in the Woolcombers County of Devon,* was presented to the House, and 1 etition. read; Setting forth. That, by the Invention of a Machine for combing of Wool, which diminishes Labour to an alarming Degree, the Petitioners entertain just Fears, that they, and their Families, will speedily become a heavy Burthen to the State, it appearing to the Petitioners, that One Machine only, with the Assistance of One Person and Four or Five Children, will perform as much Labour as Thirty Men in the

Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider further of Ways and Means fot raising the Supply granted to His Majesty, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Raising a Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, huities^An* ^lat> towards raising the Supply granted to His Majesty, the Sum of Eleven Millions be raised by Annuities, in Manner following, That is to say; That every Contributor to the said Eleven Millions shall, for every £. 1 oo contributed and paid, be entitled to the Principal Sum of 100 in Annuities, after the Rate of £. 3 per Centum, to commence from the 5th Day of January 1794, and to be added to, and made One Joint Stock with, the £. 3 per Centum Annuities, consolidated by the Acts of the Twenty-fifth, Twenty-eighth, Twenty-ninth, Thirty-second, and Thirty-third Years of the Reign of His late Majesty King George the Second, and by several subsequent Acts, and to be payable and transferrable at the Bank of England, at the same Time, and in the same Manner, and subject to the like Redemption by Parliament, as the said £. 3 per Centum Consolidated Annuities are payable and transferrable there: That every Contributor shall also be entitled to the further Principal Sum of £. 25 in Annuities, after the Rate of £. 4 per Centum, to commence from the loth Day of October 1793, and to be added to, and made One Joint Stock with, certain Annuities, after the Rate of £. 4 per Centum, which were consolidated by the Acts of the Twentieth, Twenty-first, Twenty-second, and Twenty-third Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, and to be payable and transferrable at the Bank of England, at the same Time, and in the same Manner, and subject to the like Redemption by Parliament, as the said £. 4 per Centum Consolidated Annuities are payable and transferrable there: That every such Contributor shall likewise be entitled to an Annuity of Eleven Shillings and Five Pence per Centum, to commence from the 1 oth Day of October 1793, and to continue for the Term of Sixty-six Years and a Quarter, and then to cease, over and above the Principal Sums of £. 100, after the Rate of £. 3 per Centum per Annum, and £. 25, after the Rate of £. 4 per Centum per Annum, in respect of every £. 100 to be contributed and paid towards raising the said Sum of Eleven Millions, which Annuity of Eleven Shillings and Five Pence per Centum, so. to continue for Sixty-six Years and a Quarter, shall be added to, and made One Joint Stock with, certain Annuities payable at the Bank of England, which were granted for the several Terms of Ninety-nine, Ninety-eight, Eighty, Seventy-eight, Seventy-seven Years, Seventy-five Years and a Half, and Sixty-nine Years and a Quarter, and were, by the Acts of the Fourth, Twentieth, and Twenty-second Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, and by several subsequent Acts, consolidated, and made One Joint Stock of Annuities, and shall be paid, payable, and transferrable, at the same Time, and in the same Manner, as the said Annuities, so consolidated by the Acts of the Fourth, Twentieth, and Twenty-second Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, are payable and transferrable at the said Bank of England: That the several Annuities, after the Rate of £. 3 per Centum, £. 4 per Centum, and Eleven Shillings and Five Pence per Centum, so to be payable as aforesaid, shall be charged and chargeable upon, and payable out of, the Consolidated Fund: That every Contributor shall, on or before the nth Day of this Instant February, make a Deposit of £.10 per Centum on such Sum as he or she shall chuse to subscribe towards raising the said NSum of Eleven Millions, with the Chief Cashier or Cashiers of the Governor and Company of the Bank of

England, as a Security for making the future Payments on or before the Days or Times herein after mentioned, that is to say;

next;

15 per Centum on or before the 13th Day of January 1795:

That all the Monies, so to be received by the said Cashier or Cashiers of the Governor and Company of the Bank of England, shall be paid into the Receipt of the Exchequer, to be applied, from Time to Time, to such Services as shall then have been voted by this House, in this Session of Parliament: That every Contributor, who shall pay in the Whole of his or her Contribution Money, towards the said Sum of Eleven Millions, at any Time on or before the 27th Day of November next, shall be allowed an Interest, by Way of Discount, after the Rate of £. 3 per Centum per Annum on the Sum so completing his or her Contribution respectively, to be computed from the Day of completing the same to the 13th Day of January 1795.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That an additional Duty of One Penny be charged for every Gallon of fermented Wort or Wash, which shall be brewed or made in that Part of Great Britain called England, for extracting Spirits, for Home Consumption, from any Malt, Corn, Grain, or Tilts, or any Mixture with the same.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,' That an additional Duty of One Penny be charged for every Gallon of Cyder or Perry, or any other Wash '. or Liquor, which shall be brewed or made as aforesaid from any Sort or Kind of British Materials (except such as are.before-mentioned) or from any Mixture therewith, for extracting Spirits for Home Consumption.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That an additional Duty of One Penny Half-penny be charged for every Gallon of fermented Wort or Wash, which shall be brewed or made as aforesaid from Molasses or Sugar, or any Mixture therewith, for extracting Spirits for Home Consumption.

Resolved, That it is' the Opinion of this Committee, That a Duty of Ten Shillings be charged upon every Ton of Slate, of the Produce of Great Britain, which shall be shipped to be carried by Sea from any Port or Place within this Kingdom to any other Port or Place within the same, and so in Proportion for any greater or less Quantity.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Duty of Two Shillings and Six Pence be charged upon every Ton of Stone, Granite, or Marble, of the Produce of Great Britain, whether for the Purpose of Building, Paving, or otherwise, which shall be shipped to be carried by Sea from any Port or Place within this Kingdom to any other Port or Place within the same, and so in Proportion for any greater or less Quantity.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the several Duties on Paper, Pasteboard, Mill-board, Scaleboard, and Glazed Paper, made in Great Britain, do cease and determine.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That an Excise Duty of Two Pence Half-penny be charged for every Pound Weight, Avoirdupois, of Paper fit or proper, or that may be used for, or applied to, the Uses or Purposes of Writing, Drawing, and Printing, or either of them, and of all Elephant Papers, and all Cartridge Papers, which shall be made in Great Britain, and so in Proportion for any greater or less Quantity.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That an Excise Duty of One Penny be charged for every Pound Weight, Avoirdupois, of coloured Papers and Whited Brown Papers (other than and except Elephant and Cartridge Papers) fit and proper for the Use or Purpose of wrapping up Goods, and not fit or proper, or capable of being used for, or applied to, the Uses or Purposes of Writing, Drawing, and Printing, or either of them, which shall be made in Great Britain, and so in Proportion for any greater or less Quantity.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That an Excise Duty of One Half-penny be charged for every Pound Weight, Avoirdupois, of Brown Paper fit and proper for the Use or Purpose of wrapping up Goods, and not fit or proper, or capable of being used for, or applied to, the Uses or Purposes of Writing, Drawing, and Printing, or either of them, which shall be made in Great Britain, and so in Proportion for any greater or less- Quantity.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That an Excise Duty of Two Pence Half-penny be charged for every Pound Weight, Avoirdupois, of every Sort or Kind of Paper not hereinbefore enumerated and described (and other than, and except Papers, commonly called and known by the Names of Sheathing Paper and Button Paper, or Button Board) which shall be made in Great Britain, and so in Proportion for any greater or less Quantity.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That an Excise Duty of Ten Shillings and Six Pence be charged for every One hundred Pounds Weight, Avoirdupois, of Pasteboard, Millboard, Scaleboard, and Glazed Paper, which shall he made in Great Britain, and so in Proportion for any greater or less Quantity.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said several Duties on Paper, Pasteboard, Millboard, Scaleboard, and Glazed Paper, respectively, made in Great Britain, be paid by the several Makers thereof.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Drawback of the said several Duties on Paper, Pasteboard, :Millboard, Scaleboard, and Glazed Paper, made in Great Britain, be allowed on the Exportation thereof as Merchandize to Foreign Parts.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the several Duties of Customs now payable on Paper, Pasteboard, Millboard, Scaleboard, and Pressing Paper (except Painted Paper and Paper Hangings for Rooms) imported into this Kingdom, do cease, determine, and be no longer paid.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Duty of Ten Pence be charged upon every Pound Weight of Paper, fit or proper, or that may be used for, or applied to, the Uses or Purposes of Writing, Drawing, and Printing, or either of them, and of all Elephant Papers, and all Cartridge Papers, which shall be imported into this Kingdom, either by the East India Company, or otherwise, and so in Proportion for any greater or less Quantity.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Duty of Four Pence be charged upon every Pound Weight of Coloured Papers and Whited Brown Papers (other than and except Elephant and Cartridge Papers) fit and proper for the Use and Purpose of wrapping up Goods, and not fit or proper, or capable of being used for, or applied to, the Uses or Purposes of Writing, Drawing, and Printing, or either of them, which shall be imported into this Kingdom, either by the East India Company, or otherwise, and so in Proportion for any greater or less Quantity.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Duty of Two Pence be charged upon every Pound Weight of all Brown Paper fit and Proper for the Use or Purpose of wrapping up Goods, and not fit or proper, or capable of being used for, or applied to, the Uses or Purposes of Writing, Drawing, and Printing, or either of them, which snail be imported into this Kingdom, either by the East India Company, or otherwise, and so in Proportion for any greater or less Quantity.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Duty of Ten Pence be charged upon every Pound Weight of every Sort or Kina of Paper, not hereinbefore enumerated and described, which shall be imported into this Kingdom, either by the East India Company, or otherwise, and so in Proportion for any greater or less Quantity.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That an additional Duty of Six Pence be charged upon every Pound Weight of Printed, Painted, or Stained Paper for Hangings, which shall be imported into this Kingdom, either by the East India Company, or otherwise, and so in Proportion for any greater or less Quantity.

31st January 1794. — Master of the Mint — with Account of Expences of the Mint in the Year 1793-

Sir,

I beg to inclose my Account for the Year 1793, and to desire you will please to lay it before the Lords Commissioners of His Majesty's Treasury: And having already received all the Monies their Lordships are authorized to issue to the Mint for the Service of that Year, I must submit to their Lordships the Means they may see fit for paying the Balance of Eighteen thousand Eight hundred Forty-foUr Pounds Twelve Shillings and Four Pence, that appears due thereon; which, I presume, will be done by Vote of Parliament.

I am,

Sir,

Your most obedient

humble Servant,

Leicester.

George Rose, Esq*.

5th February 1794. — OFFICERS of the Mint Report on Account of Expences of the Mint,

in the Year 1793.

To the Right honourable the Lords Commissioners of His Majesty's Treasury.

May it please your Lordships,

In Obedience to your Lordships Order of Reference of the 4th Instant, directing us to examine the Account of the Earl of Leicester, as Master and Worker of His Majesty's Mint, for the Year 1793, and to return the same, with our Observations thereupon;

We beg Leave to report, That, having compared the several Particulars of Charge and Discharge in the said Account with Vouchers and other Documents in this Office of the Expence incurred in that Year, we find them to agree, and the Account to be truly stated; and that the Balance of Eighteen thousand Eight hundred Forty-four Pounds Twelve Shillings and Four Pence, as expressed at the Foot of the Account, appears to be due to his Lordship; but the Means for paying it must be submitted to your Lordships great Wisdom.

We are,

May it please your Lordships,

Your Lordships

most obedient, and

most humble Servants,

Mint Office, Editf1 , Depr Ward*.

5th February 1794. John , Depr Comp'.

To prove the Allegations of the First-mentioned Petition, Mr. John Adey being examined, said, That the Roads described in the Petition, leading from the City of Norwich to the Town of Aylsham, are ruinous, and in many Places heavy, sandy, narrow, and incommodious; and that it would be very advantageous to the Public, if the said Roads were put into good and sufficient Repair, which cannot be done by the ordinary Course of Law.

And,

144

7° Februarii.

A. 1794.

And, to prove the Allegations of the Second-mentioned Petition, the Witness said, That the Branch of Road described in the Petition, is Part of the Road between the Town of Holt and the City of Norwich, and is only Three Miles in Length, or thereabouts, and communicates with the Road between Aylsham and Norwich, within about the Distance of Two Miles from the said City: — That the said Road is very incommodious for Travellers, and cannot be effectually amended and kept in Repair by the ordinary Course of Law; and that in case the intended Bill should pass into a Law, and no Provision be made therein for Relief of Travellers between Holt and the said City, they would be liable to pay Toll for only passing about Two Miles upon the intended Turnpike Road, which would be a very great Hardship upon such Travellers.

That several Public Meetings of the Gentlemen who are desirous of applying to Parliament for Power to amend the Road between the said City and the Town of Aylsham, were holden, to consider of a Bill for that Purpose, which should be the least burthensome to the Country; and at the last of such Meetings, it was unanimously resolved, That for the Relief of all Persons passing upon the said Branch of Road leading towards the said Town of Part of the said Road, for the Distance of about Three Miles, should be amended out of the Tolls to arise upon the Road between Norwich and Aylsham, and that no Turnpike should be erected, or any Toll taken, upon that Branch of Road.

And the Witness added, That all the principal Owners of Estates lying on each Side of the Road, and the Lord and Lady of the Manor of the Heath, upon which Part of the same leads, have been apprized of the Intention to include this Piece of Road in the intended Bill, and the greatest Part of them have consented thereto.

A Member present confirmed the above Evidence.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for amending, widening, and keeping in Repair, the Road from Norwich to Aylsham, in the County of Norfolk, and a certain Part of the Road leading from the said Road towards Holt, in the said County: And that Mr. Hobart and Sir John Wodehouse do prepare, and bring in, the same.

Mr. Praed reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Company of Proprietors of The Grand Junction Canal, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Navigation Bilk, had been complied with; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the same, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, an Act, passed in the Thirty-third Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal from the Oxford Canal Navigation, at Braunston, in the County of Northampton, to join Vol. 49.

the River Thames, at or near Brentfin the County of Middlesex, and also certain Collateral Cuts from the said intended Canal, was read: And,

William Jessop, Esquire, being examined, said, That the Petitioners are now proceeding to make the said Canal, agreeable to the Powers vested in them by the said Act.

That by Levels and Surveys, lately made, it appears practicable to make certain Navigable Cuts from the several Towns of Buckingham, Aylesbury, and dover, in the County of Buckingham, and also from the Town of Saint Alban, in the County of Hertford, to join and communicate with the said Grand Junction Canal and Collateral Cuts, or some of them.

And the Witness further said, That the making and maintaining such Navigable Cuts as aforesaid, together with proper Railways and Roads to communicate therewith, would afford the Inhabitants of the several Towns and Places, lying near the intended Cuts, a much, more regular and better Supply of Coals, Merchandize,

Corn, and Manure, and various other Articles, and at a much less Expence than at present, and that the making the said Cuts would, in other Respects, be of Public Utility.

Acton Chaplin, Esquire, One of the principal Agents to the said Grand Junction Company, being examined, said, That the said Company are willing, at their own Expence, to make and maintain the said several Navigable Cuts: And he added, That it is expedient there should be One separate Bill for the intended Cuts from Buckingham, Aylesbury, and Wendover, and

another separate Bill for the intended Cut from the Town of Saint Alban: — And the Witness further said.

That the said Act is in some Respects defective, and requires to be altered and amended.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, an Act, passed in the Thirty-second Year of His present Majesty, for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal from Kirkby Kendal, in the County of Westmorland, to West Houghton, in the County Palatine of Lancaster; and also a Navigable Branch from the said intended Canal, at or near B to or near War ton Cragg, and also another Navigable Branch, from, at, or near, Gale Moss, by Chorley, to or near Duxbury, in the said County Palatine of Lancaster, was read; w'hereby it appeared, that the Petitioners were united into a Company for the Purpose of making a Canal, to be called The Lancaster Canal, and in order to carry so useful an Undertaking into Execution, they were empowered to raise the several Sums of Money mentioned in the Act. — Then,

Another Act of the Thirty-third Year of His present Majesty's Reign, to alter and amend the above-mentioned Act, was also read; by which it appeared, that the said Company were empowered to make and maintain a certain other Navigable Branch from the said Lancaster Canal, commencing at or near Galgate, through the several Townships of Ellel and to be continued to, and communicate with, the Dock at Glassoti, within the Port of LancasterAnd,

Mr. John Rennie, an Engineer and Surveyor, being examined, said, That the said Lancaster Canal Navigation hath been proceeded in with great Expedition. — He further said. That, by a Survey he hath taken, it appears that an Extension of the said Navigation may be made from the said Lancaster Canal, in the Township of Aspul, in the Parish of- Wigan, to join and communicate with the Duke of Bridgewater's, Canal, in the Township of Worsley, in the Parish of Eccles, in the said County Palatine of Lancaster; which said Extension, by passing through the several Townships and Parishes mentioned in the Petition, will not only be of great Benefit to the Petitioners, and to all other Persons having Lands and Estates in the Neighbourhood thereof, but also to the Public in general; as it will not only open an easy, safe, and commodious Communication through a populous and trading Country, but also will unite the whole Lancaster Canal Navigation, and the several Branches thereof, rich in Coals, Cannel, and Limestone, with most of the Canal Navigations now made or making in the more Southern Parts of the Kingdom.

And being further examined, he said, That if a short Deviation of the Line of the Canal which is yet unfinished, w'as made from or near a Place called Cabus Nook, to communicate with the said Lancaster Canal Navigation, in the Township of Barnacre with Bonds, it would facilitate the making of the said Canal Navigation, and save a very considerable Expence, and would otherwise be of Public Advantage. — And the Witness further said, That in order to make the said Extension and Deviation, and to complete the said Lancaster Canal and Branches, it ma^ become necessary that the Company be empowered to borrow and take up at Interest a further Sum of Money upon the Credit of the said Lancaster Canal Navigation. — And he added, That the said Acts are in many Respects defective, and will require to be amended and rendered more effectual.
